name: SE_ReadText
semantics: Arg forms by argc. argc==1: page=0, id=arg1. argc==2: page=arg1, id=arg2, language=current (EngineConfig+0x76c). argc==3: page=arg1, LANGUAGE=arg2 (index into vm textPages), id=arg3. Found: result = CopyCell of the stored text cell (a string cell). Not found, or textPages[lang] is NULL: result is a freshly built string 'ReadText<id>' (argc 1), 'ReadText<page>-<id>' (argc 2), 'ReadText<page>-<lang>-<id>' (argc 3) (%d formatting of the raw int values, SprintfBuf50 so max 49 chars). Values are read as raw dwords, types are not checked. Sync.
notes: Text lookup: Gui::FindTextEntryInPage(textPages[lang], page, id) = hash on page id, then binary search by text id; returns the entry's payload cell. textPages[] is vm+0x334, 'lang' index = EngineConfig+0x76c (current language) unless given. Note the argc==3 order: (page, language, id); the language is arg 2, not arg 1. Strings returned from the page are NOT run through ExpandTextReferences.

name: SE_ExistsText
semantics: Same argument forms and lookup as SE_ReadText (argc 1: page 0,id; argc 2: page,id with current language; argc 3: page,lang,id). If the entry is found the result is a CopyCell of the text cell itself (the string, NOT int 1). If not found or textPages[lang] is NULL the result is int 0. No fallback string.
notes: Text lookup: Gui::FindTextEntryInPage(textPages[lang], page, id) = hash on page id, then binary search by text id; returns the entry's payload cell. textPages[] is vm+0x334, 'lang' index = EngineConfig+0x76c (current language) unless given. So the script-visible truthiness is: found -> the (usually non-empty) string; missing -> 0.

name: SE_StringLen
semantics: arg1 via CellGetString (type 2 pool string or type 0xb heap string, else NULL). NULL -> 0. Otherwise strlen in BYTES (UTF-8 bytes, not characters; SE_StringNumChars is the char counter). Sync.

name: SE_StringStr
semantics: Either of arg1/arg2 not a string -> -1. If argc>2: start=arg3 (unsigned compare); if start >= strlen(hay) (so also any negative start) -> -1; argc<=2: start=0. Then CRT strstr(hay+start, needle): result = byte offset of the match from the START OF hay (not from start) or -1 if not found. Empty needle matches immediately, result = start. Case sensitive. Sync.

name: SE_StringChr
semantics: arg1 not a string -> -1. If argc>2: start=arg3; start>=strlen (unsigned, negatives too) -> -1. Then CRT strchr(s+start, (char)ch): ch is truncated to its low byte; result = byte offset from the start of s, or -1. ch==0 (or ch&0xff==0) matches the terminator and returns strlen(s) (when start<strlen). Case sensitive. Sync.

name: SE_StringSub
semantics: s not a string -> ''. n=strlen(s); start is compared UNSIGNED: start>=n (incl. negatives) -> ''. argc<3 -> s[start:]. argc>=3: len unsigned; if len>=n or start+len>=n -> s[start:] (negative len also gives the rest). Otherwise len bytes from start, but if len!=0 the length is extended forward while the byte at s[start+len] is a UTF-8 continuation byte (&0xC0==0x80), so a multibyte char is never cut; len==0 -> ''. Returns a new string cell. Sync.
notes: Result is built with SetCellStringDup(ptr,len) in the extended case, plain copy of the tail otherwise.

name: SE_StringToInt
semantics: Only if arg1.type is 2 or 0xb: result = CRT atol(string) (leading whitespace, optional sign, decimal digits, stops at first non-digit; garbage -> 0; MSVC atol does not clamp, overflow wraps in 32 bits). Any other cell type (int, double, array...) -> 0. Sync.

name: SE_StringSubst
semantics: If any of the three is not a string (CellGetString NULL): result = CopyCell of arg1 unchanged (whatever type it was). If s does not contain find: result = CopyCell of arg1 unchanged (same cell, pool-string stays type 2). Else: all non-overlapping occurrences left-to-right are replaced by repl (scanning resumes after each match, replaced text is not rescanned); result is a new heap string. Case sensitive.
notes: Empty 'find' makes strstr return s itself every time: the loop never advances, overflows the buffer / hangs (buffer = max(len(s), (len(repl)+1-len(find))*len(s))+1). Do not emulate; treat as undefined.

name: SE_SPrintf
semantics: Result = new string = Script::FormatString(fmt, args[2..argc], nargs=argc-1) (computed twice: first for length, then filled). fmt not a string -> ''. Spec: %[!N][flags][width][.prec][h|l|L]conv. '%!N' (N one digit 0-9) selects explicit zero-based argument N (relative to the args after fmt) and does not advance the argument counter; otherwise args are consumed in order. flags: space(8) # + - 0. width/precision: digits or '*' (takes next arg: int cell value if type 1 else 0; negative width => left-justify). '.' alone => precision 0. conv: d i (signed), u x X o (unsigned; 'h' => 16 bit), integer value = arg.value ONLY if the cell type is 1 (int), else 0 (so a string/double/array arg prints 0; a missing arg (index>=nargs) prints 0). e E f F g G: double read ONLY if cell type is 0xe, else 0.0 (ints are NOT converted: %f of an int prints 0.0). c: char = low byte of int arg (type 1 else 0 -> a NUL byte). s: type 2 or 0xb string; any other type or missing arg -> literal '<invalid>'; precision truncates, width pads with spaces. a: debug dump of any cell (Script::ValueToDebugString with depth=maxelems=INT_MAX): int '%d', pool string 'text' in SINGLE quotes, heap string "text" in DOUBLE quotes, array {e1,e2,..} ({} if empty, lazy untouched arrays print {0,0,..}), table [k:v,k:v,..] in iteration order ([] if empty), double %g, object '<object N>' / '<object null>', function ref '[%06x]...', other '<type N>'; missing arg -> '[NULL]'. '%%' -> '%'. Unknown conversion char X -> the two characters '%X' are copied; a lone '%' at end of string -> '%'. Length modifier l/h/L accepted; 'l' only changes which path reads the int (same value). No locale; float formatting is the CRT style via BuildFloatFormat. Sync.
notes: Helpers: FormatString 0x004a6d80, FormatArgInt 0x004a6d10, FormatArgString 0x004a6d30, ValueToDebugString 0x004a94f0, BuildFloatFormat/FormatInteger not read in detail (assumed C printf semantics incl. flags). The result cell is type 0xb. Each arg is read at args+5*idx without regard for argc>nargs only via the idx<nargs check.

name: SE_ArrayAlloc
semantics: Result = SetCellArray(resultcell, n.value) (raw dword, type not checked): a new array of n elements, refcount 1. It is 'lazy': storage is not allocated until the first element access, and then EVERY element is initialised to int 0 (cell type 1, value 0). So all elements read as int 0 (never empty/NULL type 0). n==0 gives an empty array that behaves as size 0. n<0 (as signed): SetCellArray fails, result cell is left untouched = an empty cell (type 0), the task is resumed with that. Huge n: allocation failure => same as failure. Sync.
notes: Array object: +0 id, +4 refs, +8 size (stored as -n while lazy), +0xc capacity, +0x10 cells. Array cells hold refs (arrays/tables/strings are shared by CopyCell with refcount, not deep-copied; doubles (0xe) and int64 (0xd) are deep copied).

name: SE_ArraySize
semantics: ArrayGetSize(arg1): abs(size) if arg1.type==8 and the array pointer is non-NULL, else 0 (any non-array argument => 0, no error). Lazy arrays report their real element count. Sync.

name: SE_ArrayClone
semantics: n=ArraySize(a) (0 for non-array). Result = NEW array of n elements (lazy alloc), then for i=n-1 down to 0: dst[i]=CopyCell(src[i]) via ArrayGetElement (this MATERIALISES a lazy source: all elements become int 0). CopyCell semantics: ints/pool strings copied by value; heap strings, arrays, tables and objects are shared (refcount++), i.e. SHALLOW clone; doubles deep copied. Non-array arg => empty array. Sync.

name: SE_ArraySubClone
semantics: start=arg2, end=arg3 (raw dwords; arg3 is read even if argc<3). n=ArraySize(a). If end<0 or end>n then end=n. If start<end: result = new array of (end-start) elements with dst[j]=CopyCell(src[start+j]) (shallow, same as ArrayClone; element at an out-of-range index, e.g. start<0, becomes int 0). If start>=end: result is the INT 0 (not an empty array!). Non-array arg: n=0 so end=0, start>=0 => int 0. Half-open range [start,end).

name: SE_ArrayAppend
semantics: Script::ArrayInsert(-1, arg1, &arg2): appends a CopyCell of arg2 as the new last element (size+1). Non-array arg1 / NULL array: nothing happens. Always returns int 0 regardless of success. Capacity grows by 8 cells at a time; a lazy array just grows its virtual size and then materialises (all other elements int 0). Value is stored by CopyCell (heap objects shared by refcount). Sync.

name: SE_ArrayRemove
semantics: Script::ArrayRemove(arg1, arg2): removes the element at index (0-based): the element is destroyed, later elements shift down by one, size-1. Valid only for 0<=index<size; out of range (incl. negative, index==size) or non-array: silently nothing. Removing the last remaining element frees the storage (size 0). Lazy array: size shrinks by one regardless of index (all elements are int 0). ALWAYS returns int 0 (ArrayRemove's own -1 / 0 is discarded). Sync.

name: SE_ArrayResize
semantics: Script::ArrayResize(arg1, arg2): no-op if arg1 is not an array, array pointer NULL, or n<0 (signed). n==size: nothing. Grow: new cells are int 0 (type 1, value 0). Shrink: tail cells destroyed (refs released). n==0 frees storage (size 0). Lazy array: just sets its virtual size to n. Result is ALWAYS int 0 (the handler jumps to the 'return 0' exit). Sync.

name: SE_TableAlloc
semantics: Result = SetCellNewTable: a new empty table (type 9), refcount 1, bucketCount=4, bucket array NULL until the first insert, count 0. Arguments ignored. Sync.
notes: Table object: +8 buckets ptr, +0xc bucket count (power of 2), +0x14 entry count. Node 0x10 bytes: +0 next, +4 key cell, +9 value cell.

name: SE_TableSize
semantics: TableCount(arg1): number of entries (table object +0x14) if arg1.type==9 with non-NULL object, else 0. Sync.

name: SE_TableAdd
semantics: argc==2: table[key]=key (the value is the key cell itself). argc!=2 (3): table[key]=value. Insert-or-overwrite: Script::TableSet; existing key => value cell replaced via CopyCell (key kept), count unchanged; new key => node appended at the TAIL of its bucket chain, count+1. Returns int 1 if arg1 is a table with non-NULL object (even when overwriting), 0 otherwise (nothing done). KEY RULES: only int (type 1) and string (type 2/0xb, compared by content, case sensitive, pool and heap strings equal) keys are ever found again. Key of any other type (double, array, table, object, empty) hashes to bucket 0 and never compares equal, so every add of such a key appends a NEW unfindable duplicate node (TableExists/TableFind/TableRemove cannot reach it, but it is listed by TableKeys/TableNext). An int key never equals a string key (3 != '3'). Growth: after the insert, if count >= 4*bucketCount (i.e. bucketCount*4-1 < count) the table is rehashed to 2*bucketCount: old buckets are walked 0..n-1, each chain front to back, and each node is pushed at the HEAD of its new chain (so relative order inside a chain is reversed). Hash: int -> key & (buckets-1) (two's complement); string -> h=0; for each BYTE c (unsigned): h = c + 2*h (32-bit wrap); h & (buckets-1). Other types -> 0.
notes: Both Set (0x004a7630), Rehash (0x004a77e0), HashKey (0x004aabe0) read in full. Iteration order = ascending bucket index, then chain order.

name: SE_TableExists
semantics: If arg1.type==9: 1 if TableFindEntry(table,key) finds a node (same key rules as TableAdd: only int and string keys can match), else 0. Non-table arg1 => 0. Sync.

name: SE_TableNext
semantics: Iterates keys. argc==1: start. argc>=2: prev = arg2 only if CellIsTrue(arg2), else start. CellIsTrue is false for int 0, empty cell, pool string with offset 0, NULL refs, double 0.0 (a heap string or non-zero int is true; an EMPTY heap string "" is still true because it tests the pointer) => prevkey of int 0 (or 0.0) means START again. TableNextEntry: if arg1 is not a table / object NULL / bucket array NULL (empty table) -> result int 0. Otherwise: find the node of prev (TableFindEntry); if prev==start or the key is NOT FOUND (removed, never existed, or of an unfindable type such as double/object) -> scan restarts at bucket 0 and returns the FIRST key again. If found: next = node->next in the same chain; else the first non-empty bucket with index > prev's bucket (bucket from hash of prev, with the current bucket count). End of table -> int 0. Result = CopyCell of the next KEY cell (int or string key). => If the script removes the key it is currently standing on (the prevkey) before calling TableNext, iteration RESTARTS from the beginning (infinite loop risk); removing other keys is safe; inserting during iteration may rehash and reorder (rehash happens when count reaches 4*buckets). ORDER: buckets ascending (bucket index = hash & (n-1), n=4 initially, doubling), chain order inside a bucket = insertion order (tail append) unless the table was rehashed (chains reversed per rehash relative to old traversal order, see SE_TableAdd). Int keys 0..k in a fresh table therefore iterate in an interleaved order (bucket 0: 0,4,8..; bucket 1: 1,5,..), NOT insertion order. Sync.
notes: TableNextEntry 0x004aace0, CellIsTrue 0x004a8970, TableFindEntry 0x004aa9f0, TableHashKey 0x004aabe0. Verified in dis (CMP argc,1; LEA ESI,[EDI+5]; CALL CellIsTrue).

name: SE_TableRemove
semantics: TableFindValue(table,key): if arg1 is not a table or the key is absent (only int/string keys findable) -> result int 0 and nothing is changed. If present: result = CopyCell of the stored VALUE cell (the value that was removed, NOT a 1/0 flag), then the node is unlinked from its chain, key and value cells destroyed, count-1. Bucket array is never shrunk. NOTE the result is indistinguishable from 'absent' when the stored value was int 0. Sync.

name: SE_TableKeys
semantics: n=TableCount(arg1) (0 for non-table). Result = new array of n (lazy alloc) filled with the keys in TableNext iteration order (starting at the beginning, each step TableNextEntry(prevkey)), each key CopyCell'd. Because each step re-finds the previous key by lookup, unfindable key types (double/object/array duplicates) make the walk restart at the first key. Non-table or empty => empty array. Sync.

name: SE_GetTaskID
semantics: Result = id of the calling task (task+8). Sync.

name: SE_KillTask
semantics: FreeTaskById(arg1.value): looks the id up in the VM task hash; if a task exists it is freed (killed) at once; unknown id => nothing. Then the caller's own id is looked up again (the helper named Cockpit::FindByHandle is really the task-by-id lookup, also used by SE_TaskExists): if the calling task still exists it is resumed with int 0; if the caller killed ITSELF, no result is delivered and the dispatcher returns 0 (step aborted, scheduler yields to the next frame; the task is gone). Normal result: int 0. Arg type is not checked.

name: SE_ObjectExists
semantics: CellIsValidObject(arg1): if type 0xa (object ref): 1 iff the ref pointer is non-NULL and its object context pointer (+8) is non-NULL (object not destroyed), else 0. If type 1 (int): non-zero value => ResolveObjectContext(id) != 0 -> 1/0 (negative ids look up script-created objects, non-negative ids static class table); int 0 => 0. Any other type => 0. Sync.

name: SE_IsClass
semantics: If CellIsTrue(arg1) is false -> 0. ctx = arg1.value if arg1.type==0xa else ResolveObjectContext(arg1.value) (so an int, or even a string cell, is treated as an object id). ctx==0 -> 0. Then if arg2.type==0xa (class reference): arg2's class pointer must be self-consistent (cls==cls->self) else 0; result 1 iff that class is in the object's class chain (the object's own class or any ancestor via parent pointer +0x14). Else (arg2 not a class ref): ObjectIsOfClass(ctx, arg2.value): 1 iff some class in the object's class chain (own or any ancestor) has id (class+0) == arg2.value. So subclass objects satisfy IsClass for their superclasses. Result 1/0. Sync.

name: SE_GetExprType
semantics: Result = the raw type byte of the argument cell: 0 empty, 1 int, 2 pool string (script string constant/text), 3 function/frame ref, 8 array, 9 table, 0xa object ref, 0xb heap string (runtime built string), 0xc/0xd int64 boxed, 0xe double, 0xf other. NO normalisation: a literal string constant is 2, the same text after SE_StringSub/concatenation is 0xb. Sync. (SE_IsString returns 1 for types 2 and 0xb.)

name: SE_LinFunc
semantics: Clamped linear interpolation, all 32-bit ints: args = (x0=arg1, x1=arg2, y0=arg3, y1=arg4, x=arg5) passed to ClampedLinearRamp(x, x1, y1, x0, y0). if x0==x1: (y0+y1)/2 (C trunc division). elif x<=x0: y0. elif x>=x1: y1. else if x<0x10000 (signed) and (x1-x0)<0x10000 (signed): (y0+y1)/2 + MulDiv(y1-y0, 2*x-x0-x1, 2*(x1-x0)) else (y0+y1)/2 + (int)(((int64)(y1-y0)*(int64)(x-(x1+x0)/2))/(int64)(x1-x0)). MulDiv = IDIV based a*b/c truncating toward zero, c==0 -> 0 (64/32-bit IDIV: quotient overflow of 32 bits would raise a divide exception). Sync.
notes: Argument order verified from the push sequence at 0x004ace96 (ESI=arg3 pushed first, EDX=arg1 second; EAX=arg2, EDI=arg4, ECX=arg5). Note (x1+x0)/2 and 2*x-x0-x1 use 32-bit wrapping arithmetic.

name: SE_DistanceAA
semantics: arg1 and arg2 are arrays of 3 int cells (x,y,z). All six ArrayGetElement(.,0..2) must be non-NULL (index in range, arrays valid, lazy arrays materialise to int 0) else result int 0. The int payload (cell+1) is read without checking the cell type. dx=a0-b0, dy=a1-b1, dz=a2-b2 (32-bit wrapping int subtraction). Result = VecLengthToInt(float(dx),float(dy),float(dz)) = (int)sqrt(float32(dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz)): x87 evaluation, the sum is stored as a 32-bit FLOAT before FSQRT, then truncation toward zero (Crt::Ftol). Sync.
notes: Float32 precision limits: exact for results < ~4000; larger distances can differ by 1 from an exact integer sqrt. Emulate with float32 rounding of the converted inputs' squares sum.

name: SE_MulFix
semantics: 16.16 fixed multiply: ((int64)a*(int64)b + 0x8000) >> 16 (arithmetic shift of the signed 64-bit sum), low 32 bits returned as signed int (IMUL; ADD 0x8000; ADC; SHRD 16). Rounds half up. Overflow wraps in 32 bits. Sync.

name: SE_DivFix
semantics: 16.16 fixed divide: b==0 -> 0. Else ((int64)a<<16) / b with a 64-bit IDIV (EDX:EAX / ECX), truncating toward zero, remainder dropped (no rounding). If the quotient does not fit in 32 bits (|a/b| >= 32768.0 in 16.16, i.e. |(a<<16)/b| >= 2^31) the CPU raises #DE (integer divide exception) - the exe does not guard it; the emulator should treat it as a crash. Sync.

name: SE_MulDivFix
semantics: Math::MulDiv(a,b,c): c==0 -> 0. Else (int)(((int64)a*(int64)b)/c) via IMUL then IDIV ECX (64/32): truncates toward zero; if the quotient exceeds 32 bits the CPU raises #DE (unguarded). Pure integer: no 16.16 scaling is applied despite the name. Sync.

name: SE_Random
semantics: n<1 (signed) -> 0. Else Math::RandScaled(n) = (int)(((int64)n * rand()) / 0x8000) using the MSVC CRT rand() (0..32767): result in [0, n-1]. Uses the shared CRT generator (seeded elsewhere by the engine); sequence cannot be reproduced exactly, emulator may use any uniform integer in [0,n-1]. Sync.

name: SE_QSortByName
semantics: Script::ArraySortRangeByString(a, keys, start, end, desc) with desc = (argc>=5 && arg5!=0). Silently does nothing unless both args are arrays (non-NULL) and 0<=start<end<size(a) AND end<size(keys) (end is INCLUSIVE; start==end, single element, is also a no-op). Otherwise: builds records for indices start..end of {key string = text of keys[i] (CellGetString: only string cells 2/0xb, any other type counts as ''), copy of a[i]}, sorts them with MSVC qsort using case-insensitive _stricmp ascending (descending when desc: operands swapped), NULL/non-string keys first (asc) / last (desc), and writes the sorted copies back into a[start..end]. keys[] is NOT reordered (pass the same array twice to sort strings in place). qsort is not stable: equal keys (case-insensitive) have unspecified relative order (MSVC qsort: quicksort, insertion sort for small partitions). Always returns int 0. Sync.

name: SE_ConvertFormatString
semantics: arg1 not a string -> int 0. If the string contains no '{' character: result = CopyCell of arg1 unchanged. Otherwise result = new string from Gui::ExpandTextReferences(s): every top-level balanced {page,id} (page and id decimal numbers; first char after '{' and after ',' must be a digit; atol each; page!=0) is replaced by the text GetText(page,id) of the CURRENT language, itself recursively expanded (nested {..} in that text). Any '{...}' that is not of that shape (no comma before the matching '}', non-digit start, page==0) is left in the output unchanged; an unbalanced '{' leaves the rest of the string as is. Missing text gives whatever Gui::GetText returns for a miss (the engine placeholder text). Sync.
notes: Handler only inspected via dis (strchr 0x7b then ExpandTextReferences 0x004ab320); ExpandTextReferences decompiled, brace matching logic summarised from that decompile (medium confidence on details of the literal-keep paths).

name: TI_Delay
semantics: Suspends the calling task. delay = arg1 if argc!=2, or arg1*1000+arg2 if argc==2 (units: game-clock milliseconds, the clock is EngineConfig+0x718, the same as TI_GetAbsTime). A timer node is queued with due = clock + delay + jitter, jitter = rand()*min(delay/16+1, 256)/0x8000 for delay<0x1000 (i.e. 0..delay/16), else 0..255 (so the wait is slightly LONGER than requested, never shorter); negative delay gives jitter 0 (delay/16+1 <= 0 -> 0) and fires on the next tick. TiTick (every frame, before script run) fires every node with (due - clock) <= 0, resuming the task with int 0. The task wakes on a LATER frame (not the same frame). A killed task id is ignored when the timer fires.
notes: TiDispatch 0x004b1300; TiScheduleDelay 0x004b0b00; TiTick 0x004b0e00. Dispatcher returns 1 without calling ResumeTask (the task waits). Fires also when time warp advances the clock.

name: TI_DelayRandom
semantics: Like TI_Delay with delay = arg1 + (arg2>0 ? RandScaled(arg2) = rand()*arg2/0x8000 : 0), i.e. arg1 + [0, arg2-1] (arg2<=0 => delay=arg1). Always the two-argument (base,range) form; arg2 is NOT seconds. Plus the TiScheduleDelay jitter. Wakes with int 0.

name: TI_GetAbsTime
semantics: Result = EngineConfig+0x718 = the game clock (ms, scaled by time warp; set by TI_SetAbsTime, advanced each frame). Sync.

name: TI_CmpTime
semantics: Result = t1 - t2 as a plain 32-bit wrapping subtraction (arg1 - arg2). No clock access. Sync.

name: TI_GetRealTime
semantics: Result = EngineConfig+0x720 (real, un-warped elapsed time in ms-units; the counterpart of TI_GetAbsTime). Sync.
notes: Unit/epoch of +0x720 inferred only from the name; field not traced to its writer.

name: TI_Interrupt
semantics: TiSignalInterrupt(key): walks the delayed-timer list; every node flagged 'waiting for interrupt' (created by TI_WaitForInterrupt / TI_WaitRandomForInterrupt) whose key == arg1 is completed NOW: its task is resumed with int value = remaining time (due - clock, ms, may be <=0), and the node is removed. Tasks in plain TI_Delay are not affected. Then the caller itself continues with int 0 (not suspended). Wakeups run through the group completion callback (ResumeTask: the woken tasks are put at the head of the runnable list). Sync.
notes: TI_WaitForInterrupt(delay,key) wakes with 0 on timeout and with remaining ms on interrupt.
